newsitem.title: USA: General Mills Q4 EPS seen down - analysts.
newsitem.headline: General Mills Q4 EPS seen down - analysts.

text.p: A tough comparison with year-ago sales and an expected decline in domestic cereal volume will result in softer earnings for General Mills Inc in the fiscal fourth quarter, analysts said.

"This is going to be a very poor quarter for General Mills," Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said, adding she expects the Minneapolis-based food company to post earnings of $0.42 a share, down from $0.49 a year ago.
The First Call mean estimate for the fourth quarter ended in May is $0.44 a share, based on a range of $0.40 to $0.52.
Beyond that, General Mills faces a difficult comparison with the year-ago fourth quarter, when sales volume benefited from the launch of promotions tied to the 1996 Summer Olympics.

In the 1997 fourth quarter, General Mills' promotions were tied to "The Lost World," the sequel to the movie "Jurassic Park." In keeping with the film's storyline, several General Mills products featured dinosaur themes.
"I guess dinosaurs are not as popular as the Olympics when it comes to cereal," Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette analyst William Leach said.
Leach said he expected General Mills' Big G cereal division to show about a three percent decline in volume.
Ghez said she expected fourth-quarter cereal volume to be off one to two percent, with a slight increase overall for the full year.
Overall, the U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market, in which General Mills is the No. 2 player behind Kellogg Co, is sluggish, growing by one to two percent, analysts said.
